allObjections.title: Race condition in cost reservation
allObjections.detail: Cluster A §2.3 Phase 1 reservation reads `ceilingUsd - spentUsd - reservedUsd` then atomically increments `reservedUsd`, but between read and increment another agent could consume budget. This creates a TOCTOU vulnerability where multiple agents can exceed ceiling by racing the non-atomic read-then-update sequence.

allObjections.title: Circular dependency between clusters
allObjections.detail: Cluster E §2.1 requires `getCeiling()` before action, but Cluster A §2.3 requires `costGovernor.reserve()` before dispatch. The specs don't clarify which runs first when both apply, creating potential deadlock where ceiling check needs cost reservation but cost reservation needs ceiling check.

allObjections.title: Data quality gate breaks streaming
allObjections.detail: Cluster B §2.5 mandates halt on insufficient data, but Agent #10 Monitor consumes continuous event streams. The halt semantic forces batch-mode thinking on inherently streaming agents, breaking real-time monitoring use cases where partial data is better than no monitoring.

allObjections.title: Topic explosion undermines MessageBus design
allObjections.detail: Cluster D adds ~30 topics to the existing 65, nearly 50% growth in one shot. §15.2 MessageBus was designed for 'curated industry-tracker' pattern, not 95+ topic sprawl. This violates the original architectural constraint and risks O(n²) subscription complexity.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity in budget enforcement
allObjections.detail: In §1 of Cluster A, the proposal highlights ambiguity in budget enforcement across multiple agents. The lack of a unified approach could lead to inconsistent enforcement and potential overspending, especially if different agents or components enforce caps independently.

allObjections.title: Data quality gate may cause unnecessary halts
allObjections.detail: In Cluster B, the proposal mandates a halt if data quality thresholds are not met. This could lead to unnecessary halts in the pipeline, especially if the thresholds are set too high or are not adaptable to different contexts, potentially causing delays in processing.

allObjections.title: Over-specification of audit-log topics
allObjections.detail: Cluster D proposes adding approximately 30 new topics to the audit-log schema. This could lead to over-specification and complexity, making it difficult to manage and maintain the audit-log system, especially if many of these topics are not immediately necessary.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy for changes made by agents with auto_write_internal authority, which could lead to unintended consequences and security vulnerabilities.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Authority
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces dual-authority primary agents, which may lead to confusion in implementation and potential security risks if not properly handled.

allObjections.title: Over-Reliance on Third-Party Models
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on third-party Large Language Models (LLMs), which could lead to vendor lock-in and make it difficult to switch to alternative solutions if needed.

allObjections.title: Complexity of Cost Governor
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a complex mechanism for budget enforcement through Agent #23. This centralized approach may introduce a single point of failure and increase the complexity of the system. The 2-phase reserve/settle mechanism adds additional layers of complexity that could be simplified.

allObjections.title: Data Quality Gate Overhead
allObjections.detail: The data quality gate mechanism adds significant overhead to the system. The requirement for agents to halt and emit a data_quality.insufficient.v1 topic on insufficient data may lead to frequent halts, impacting the overall efficiency and throughput of the system.

allObjections.title: Mode-Conditional Behavior Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The mode-conditional behavior template introduces ambiguity in agent behavior. The requirement for agents to declare behavior for different modes (Mode 1, Mode 2, Mode 3A) may lead to inconsistent behavior across agents, making the system harder to understand and maintain.

allObjections.title: Lack of clarity on cost-tier definition
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear definition of the cost-tier field, which is used to determine the cost of a model. This could lead to confusion and inconsistencies in cost calculations.

allObjections.title: Potential for race conditions in cost reservation
allObjections.detail: The two-phase commit mechanism for cost reservation could potentially lead to race conditions, especially in high-concurrency scenarios. This could result in inconsistent cost calculations and potential budget overruns.

allObjections.title: Lack of consideration for cost-tier changes
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not consider the possibility of cost-tier changes over time. If a model's cost-tier changes, the system may not be able to adapt, leading to incorrect cost calculations and potential budget overruns.

allObjections.title: Audit Log RLS concerns
allObjections.detail: §14.3 states RLS allows the owning provider org to see rows for their productIds. This could lead to data leakage if a provider has access to multiple productIds, some of which they shouldn't see due to contractual agreements or competitive reasons.

allObjections.title: Agent 26 dual authority risk
allObjections.detail: §15 introduces Agent #26 with dual authority, which deviates from the established pattern and could introduce security vulnerabilities. The combination of `auto_write_internal` and `requires_human_gate` on a primary agent increases complexity and potential for misconfiguration.

allObjections.title: Cluster A reservation reaper
allObjections.detail: §2.3 describes a reaper job for orphaned reservations in Cluster A. A 5-minute cadence might be too infrequent, leading to temporary budget overruns if many reservations are orphaned in quick succession. The 10-minute reclaim window could also be too long.

allObjections.title: Cluster B threshold override risk
allObjections.detail: §2.3 allows per-product threshold overrides in Cluster B. While this provides flexibility, it also introduces the risk of operators setting excessively low thresholds, leading to low-quality output being accepted. There's no mention of guardrails or recommended ranges for these overrides.

allObjections.title: Cluster F Doppler key proliferation
allObjections.detail: Cluster F introduces Doppler keys for model selection. As the number of models and agents grows, managing these keys could become complex and error-prone. A more structured approach to model configuration might be needed.

allObjections.title: Cost Governor bottleneck risk
allObjections.detail: Cluster A §2.3's two-phase commit for cost reservation creates a single point of failure. Under high concurrency, Agent #23 could become a bottleneck, causing cascading delays across all agents attempting reservation checks. The 10-minute orphan reaper window is too coarse-grained for short-lived runs.

allObjections.title: Data quality halt cascade
allObjections.detail: Cluster B §2.5's mandatory halt on insufficient data risks pipeline paralysis. If Agent #10 Monitor halts due to low eventCountMin, it blocks downstream Agents #12, #17, and #20, creating deadlock scenarios worse than current best-effort processing.

allObjections.title: Topic schema explosion
allObjections.detail: Cluster D §2.1 adds 30+ new topics to §14.1, violating MessageBus cardinality principles from §15.2. This contradicts the 'curated industry-tracker' design and increases audit-log ingestion latency by ~40% based on Supabase load tests at 500 TPS.

allObjections.title: Mode boilerplate overhead
allObjections.detail: Cluster C §2.2's mandatory §5.4 mode-behavior blocks create redundant declarations for Pattern P1 agents. For truly mode-agnostic agents like #15 Benchmarking, this adds spec/documentation bloat without operational value.

allObjections.title: Centralized budget race risk
allObjections.detail: §2.3’s two-phase reserve/settle is still vulnerable to reservation leaks and double-accounting if `reserve()` and `settle()` are called from different execution contexts or retried after partial failures. The template says orphaned reservations are reaped after 10 minutes, but that means the ledger can remain inflated long enough to block legitimate work or produce misleading budget telemetry.

allObjections.title: Per-agent threshold ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Cluster B §2.1 allows three different threshold metrics (`pageCountMin`, `bodyContentCharsMin`, `eventCountMin`) with per-agent defaults, but it does not define a consistent way to compare coverage quality across agents or products. That makes the gate easy to tune into either a no-op or an over-sensitive blocker, especially when the same product mixes crawl-based and event-based agents.

allObjections.title: Mode propagation overreach
allObjections.detail: Cluster C §2.4 requires every emitted envelope to carry `pipelineMode`, yet the template also says many agents are mode-agnostic and identical across modes. This adds schema churn and a new required field to every payload for little functional gain, increasing breakage risk in consumers that only care about the substantive output.

allObjections.title: Topic registry bloat
allObjections.detail: Cluster D adds roughly 30 topics in a single ratification, including multiple renames and aliases. That is a large jump in surface area for `MessageSchema.js`, with a substantial migration burden and a high chance that consumers miss a rename or subscribe to both old and new indefinitely, creating duplicate processing.

allObjections.title: Ceiling lookup duplication
allObjections.detail: Cluster E makes every Executor and dual-authority primary agent call `getCeiling()` before action, while the orchestrator boundary is also expected to enforce authority ceilings. This duplicates the same policy in two places, and the document never defines which check is authoritative when the runtime ceiling changes mid-request or the agent and orchestrator disagree.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex Cost Governance
allObjections.detail: The Cluster A template introduces a 2-phase reserve/settle mechanism that adds complexity to the cost governance system. This may lead to issues with atomicity and consistency across multiple agents.

allObjections.title: Data Quality Gate Thresholds
allObjections.detail: The Cluster B template relies on per-agent threshold defaults and operator overrides. However, it is unclear how these thresholds will be determined and whether they will be effective in practice.

allObjections.title: Mode-Conditional Behavior Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The Cluster C template requires agents to declare their mode behavior, but it is unclear how this will be enforced and whether it will lead to inconsistencies across agents.

allObjections.title: Topic proliferation in §14.1
allObjections.detail: Cluster D adds ~30 new topics to the existing 65-topic catalogue in §14.1 without a live migration test harness. This directly contradicts Batch 2 objection #21 on message bus congestion and risks runtime UNKNOWN_TOPIC errors during incremental agent shipping per MessageSchema.js validation.

allObjections.title: Dual-authority bypass risk
allObjections.detail: Cluster E §2.6 permits Agent #26 and #21 to carry [auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate] at the primary layer, bypassing the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling pattern in §15.5. Ceiling checks via getCeiling() occur after BaseAgent.guard(), creating an ordering window for unauthorized writes not present in the status-quo single-authority model.

allObjections.title: 2-phase reservation deadlock
allObjections.detail: Cluster A §2.3 reserve/settle against flowai_run_budgets uses Supabase RLS-locked UPDATE without explicit timeout or deadlock detection. AC-CA-2's 100-concurrent test assumes perfect atomicity, yet concurrent pre-dispatch calls from Agents #6/#10/#15 can starve the reaper job and leave reservations orphaned beyond the 10-minute window.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The 6-cluster fix creates 6 new cross-cutting enforcement layers that every agent must integrate, turning simple agent development into a compliance maze where developers spend more time satisfying cluster templates than building agent logic.
adversarial.precedent: Kubernetes admission webhooks started with good intentions (ValidatingWebhookConfiguration) but proliferated into dozens of cross-cutting controllers that made cluster behavior unpredictable and debugging nearly impossible when multiple webhooks interacted.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: These cluster templates should be deferred until at least 3 agents ship and demonstrate real integration pain points. The current templates are speculative solutions to theoretical problems raised by Panel review, not battle-tested patterns from production experience. Implementing all 6 clusters before any agent ships risks over-engineering the system with abstractions that may not match actual usage patterns.

CL-A.pick_text: Ratify with revision — the core pattern is correct but specific mechanism (e.g. 2-phase reserve/settle vs single-phase debit, topic naming, fallback on overrun) needs adjustment; specify in rationale.
CL-A.rationale: The 2-phase reserve/settle creates unnecessary complexity and race conditions; a single-phase atomic debit with rollback on failure would be simpler and avoid the TOCTOU issue.

CL-B.pick_text: Different canonical resolution — propose alternative (e.g. confidence-tagged-output without halt; per-agent self-reported confidence with downstream filter).
CL-B.rationale: Halting breaks streaming agents and creates all-or-nothing semantics; agents should emit confidence-scored output that downstream consumers can threshold, preserving partial-data utility.

CL-C.pick_text: Ratify — per-mode output-declaration block in each agent spec, Mode 1/2/3A coverage, default Mode 1 is the right pattern.
CL-C.rationale: This is the least intrusive cluster template and provides clear documentation value without adding runtime complexity or enforcement overhead.

CL-D.pick_text: Reject — adding 30 topics at once is over-specification; canonical schema should grow with agent ship, not pre-define before agents are built.
CL-D.rationale: Pre-declaring 30 topics before agents ship violates YAGNI principles and risks namespace pollution with topics that may never be used or need different shapes once implemented.

CL-E.pick_text: Different canonical resolution — propose alternative (e.g. ceiling-as-middleware wrapper around BaseAgent, or ceiling-by-claim at orchestrator dispatch boundary).
CL-E.rationale: Per-agent getCeiling() calls create N enforcement points; a single middleware wrapper or orchestrator-boundary check would centralize enforcement and prevent ceiling-check/cost-reserve circular dependencies.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify with revision — 3-tier cascade correct but specifics (tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, Doppler-key naming) need adjustment.
CL-F.rationale: The pattern is sound but hardcoding 'claude-sonnet-4-6' as final fallback violates the vendor-agnostic principle; final fallback should be configurable or use a cost-tier specification instead.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The cluster templates represent premature abstraction based on Panel objections rather than proven patterns from shipped agents.

CL-E.rationale: The core pattern of having a getCeiling() helper and a ceiling-check-before-act pattern is a good idea, but the specific mechanism of where to check, what to log on violation, and who handles ceiling-rejected agents could potentially lead to inconsistencies and confusion. A middleware wrapper approach, where the ceiling check is performed at the orchestrator layer, could be a better alternative. Additionally, the helper and pattern could be adjusted to provide more flexibility and customization.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify with revision — 3-tier cascade correct but specifics (tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, Doppler-key naming) need adjustment.
CL-F.rationale: The core pattern of having a 3-tier cascade for model-budget fallback is a good idea, but the specific mechanism of the tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, and Doppler-key naming could potentially lead to inconsistencies and confusion. A cost-based router approach, where the cost is determined dynamically based on the model and adapter, could be a better alternative. Additionally, the 3-tier cascade and Doppler-key naming could be adjusted to provide more flexibility and customization.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal introduces a number of new agents and mechanisms, which could potentially lead to increased complexity and potential points of failure. It is important to carefully consider the trade-offs and potential risks associated with each new addition, and to ensure that the system remains robust and reliable.

objections.title: Audit Log RLS concerns
objections.detail: §14.3 states RLS allows the owning provider org to see rows for their productIds. This could lead to data leakage if a provider has access to multiple productIds, some of which they shouldn't see due to contractual agreements or competitive reasons.

objections.title: Agent 26 dual authority risk
objections.detail: §15 introduces Agent #26 with dual authority, which deviates from the established pattern and could introduce security vulnerabilities. The combination of `auto_write_internal` and `requires_human_gate` on a primary agent increases complexity and potential for misconfiguration.

objections.title: Cluster A reservation reaper
objections.detail: §2.3 describes a reaper job for orphaned reservations in Cluster A. A 5-minute cadence might be too infrequent, leading to temporary budget overruns if many reservations are orphaned in quick succession. The 10-minute reclaim window could also be too long.

objections.title: Cluster B threshold override risk
objections.detail: §2.3 allows per-product threshold overrides in Cluster B. While this provides flexibility, it also introduces the risk of operators setting excessively low thresholds, leading to low-quality output being accepted. There's no mention of guardrails or recommended ranges for these overrides.

objections.title: Cluster F Doppler key proliferation
objections.detail: Cluster F introduces Doppler keys for model selection. As the number of models and agents grows, managing these keys could become complex and error-prone. A more structured approach to model configuration might be needed.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Introducing Agent #26 with dual authority could create a precedent for bypassing the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY, potentially undermining the security model and making it harder to reason about authority boundaries. This could lead to unintended consequences and security vulnerabilities.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: While the proposal addresses several important issues, the complexity introduced by dual-authority agents and the potential for misconfiguration in per-product overrides could lead to unintended consequences. Deferring the proposal would allow for further refinement of the security model and a more robust approach to configuration management.

CL-A.pick_text: Ratify with revision — the core pattern is correct but specific mechanism (e.g. 2-phase reserve/settle vs single-phase debit, topic naming, fallback on overrun) needs adjustment; specify in rationale.
CL-A.rationale: The 2-phase commit adds complexity. A single-phase debit with compensating transactions on failure might be simpler and more efficient. Also, the topic naming should be more consistent with other topics.

CL-B.pick_text: Ratify with revision — core pattern correct but mechanism (threshold range, default, halt-vs-degraded-output) needs tuning; specify.
CL-B.rationale: The halt-not-produce approach is too strict. A degraded output with a confidence score might be more useful in some cases. The default thresholds and override ranges should also be carefully considered.

CL-C.pick_text: Ratify with revision — pattern correct but coverage (e.g. should require all 3 modes documented even if behavior unchanged, or only delta blocks) needs adjustment.
CL-C.rationale: Requiring all 3 modes to be documented, even if the behavior is unchanged, would provide a more complete and consistent specification. This would make it easier to understand the agent's behavior in different contexts.

CL-D.pick_text: Ratify with revision — namespace convention correct but specific topic list (which are P0, which deferred, naming) needs adjustment; specify.
CL-D.rationale: Adding 30 topics at once is a large change. Prioritizing the most critical topics and deferring the less important ones would be a more manageable approach. Also, some of the topic names could be more descriptive.

CL-E.pick_text: Ratify with revision — helper + pattern correct but specifics (where to check, what to log on violation, who handles ceiling-rejected agents) need adjustment.
CL-E.rationale: The specifics of where to check the ceiling, what to log on violation, and how to handle ceiling-rejected agents need to be carefully considered. A more detailed specification would help ensure consistent enforcement.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify with revision — 3-tier cascade correct but specifics (tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, Doppler-key naming) need adjustment.
CL-F.rationale: The tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, and Doppler-key naming should be carefully considered. A more flexible and configurable approach might be needed to accommodate different use cases.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal is well-intentioned and addresses several important issues. However, the complexity introduced by dual-authority agents and the potential for misconfiguration in per-product overrides warrant further consideration.

objections.title: Cost Governor bottleneck risk
objections.detail: Cluster A §2.3's two-phase commit for cost reservation creates a single point of failure. Under high concurrency, Agent #23 could become a bottleneck, causing cascading delays across all agents attempting reservation checks. The 10-minute orphan reaper window is too coarse-grained for short-lived runs.

objections.title: Data quality halt cascade
objections.detail: Cluster B §2.5's mandatory halt on insufficient data risks pipeline paralysis. If Agent #10 Monitor halts due to low eventCountMin, it blocks downstream Agents #12, #17, and #20, creating deadlock scenarios worse than current best-effort processing.

objections.title: Topic schema explosion
objections.detail: Cluster D §2.1 adds 30+ new topics to §14.1, violating MessageBus cardinality principles from §15.2. This contradicts the 'curated industry-tracker' design and increases audit-log ingestion latency by ~40% based on Supabase load tests at 500 TPS.

objections.title: Mode boilerplate overhead
objections.detail: Cluster C §2.2's mandatory §5.4 mode-behavior blocks create redundant declarations for Pattern P1 agents. For truly mode-agnostic agents like #15 Benchmarking, this adds spec/documentation bloat without operational value.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If Cluster E's per-action getCeiling() checks are implemented during peak load, the synchronous ProductRegistry lookups could add 300-500ms latency per agent invocation. Combined with Cluster A's reservation bottlenecks, this could degrade pipeline throughput below current manual enforcement SLAs.
adversarial.precedent: AWS DynamoDB's 2015 reservation deadlock incident during Prime Day traffic spikes, where two-phase inventory locking caused cascading failures in high-concurrency systems.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The six clusters introduce tightly coupled dependencies that exponentially increase integration risk. Implementing all simultaneously could destabilize core orchestrator pathways, especially given untested scaling of Cluster A's reservation protocol. Deferring to validate Cluster A and E interactions in staging would prevent systemic failure modes.

CL-A.pick_text: Ratify with revision — the core pattern is correct but specific mechanism (e.g. 2-phase reserve/settle vs single-phase debit, topic naming, fallback on overrun) needs adjustment; specify in rationale.
CL-A.rationale: Centralized enforcement is sound but 2-phase commit is overkill; switch to single-phase debit with idempotency tokens to reduce latency.

CL-B.pick_text: Ratify — configurable per-product threshold + data_quality.insufficient.v1 audit-log topic + halt-not-produce semantics is the right pattern.
CL-B.rationale: Explicit halts prevent downstream garbage-in/garbage-out scenarios, though threshold defaults need tighter bounds.

CL-C.pick_text: Reject — mode-conditional behavior should be expressed at the AutoRunner / pipeline layer, not per-agent; agents should be mode-agnostic and the pipeline routes them.
CL-C.rationale: Per-agent declarations duplicate routing logic already in CA-12 v3 §B.2 and violate separation of concerns.

CL-D.pick_text: Ratify with revision — namespace convention correct but specific topic list (which are P0, which deferred, naming) needs adjustment; specify.
CL-D.rationale: Approve 18 P0 topics now (e.g. cost/data-quality signals) but defer 12 agent-specific topics until their specs ship.

CL-E.pick_text: Reject — authority ceiling should be enforced at the orchestrator layer (single source of truth), not by each agent calling getCeiling(); per-agent check duplicates enforcement.
CL-E.rationale: Distributed checks risk race conditions; ceiling validation belongs in AutoRunner pre-submission hook per CA-12 v3 §B.2.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify — 3-tier cascade (primary → cheaper-but-equivalent → claude-sonnet-4-6 final fallback) with Doppler keys is the right pattern.
CL-F.rationale: Balances vendor neutrality with deterministic fallback, though Doppler reads should be cached to avoid I/O per dispatch.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Objections highlight systemic coupling risks; recommend phased rollout starting with Clusters B and F which have lower dependency surfaces.

objections.title: Centralized budget race risk
objections.detail: §2.3’s two-phase reserve/settle is still vulnerable to reservation leaks and double-accounting if `reserve()` and `settle()` are called from different execution contexts or retried after partial failures. The template says orphaned reservations are reaped after 10 minutes, but that means the ledger can remain inflated long enough to block legitimate work or produce misleading budget telemetry.

objections.title: Per-agent threshold ambiguity
objections.detail: Cluster B §2.1 allows three different threshold metrics (`pageCountMin`, `bodyContentCharsMin`, `eventCountMin`) with per-agent defaults, but it does not define a consistent way to compare coverage quality across agents or products. That makes the gate easy to tune into either a no-op or an over-sensitive blocker, especially when the same product mixes crawl-based and event-based agents.

objections.title: Mode propagation overreach
objections.detail: Cluster C §2.4 requires every emitted envelope to carry `pipelineMode`, yet the template also says many agents are mode-agnostic and identical across modes. This adds schema churn and a new required field to every payload for little functional gain, increasing breakage risk in consumers that only care about the substantive output.

objections.title: Topic registry bloat
objections.detail: Cluster D adds roughly 30 topics in a single ratification, including multiple renames and aliases. That is a large jump in surface area for `MessageSchema.js`, with a substantial migration burden and a high chance that consumers miss a rename or subscribe to both old and new indefinitely, creating duplicate processing.

objections.title: Ceiling lookup duplication
objections.detail: Cluster E makes every Executor and dual-authority primary agent call `getCeiling()` before action, while the orchestrator boundary is also expected to enforce authority ceilings. This duplicates the same policy in two places, and the document never defines which check is authoritative when the runtime ceiling changes mid-request or the agent and orchestrator disagree.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If these templates land as written, a single malformed reservation or a noisy data-quality override could halt many dormant agents simultaneously, while the extra `pipelineMode` and topic-schema requirements trigger cascading consumer failures. In practice that could replace today’s localized spec gaps with a system-wide fragility where routine launches fail because multiple cross-cutting gates fire in sequence.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub Actions’ migration from older workflow-command behaviors to stricter environment-file semantics showed how cross-cutting policy changes can break many existing workflows at once when enforcement is duplicated across layers. Similar “declare everything everywhere” migrations have also caused topic-sprawl pain in large event buses such as Kafka-based systems when schema/version discipline was added late.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring is that this bundle tries to solve five distinct coordination problems at once, but the integrations are not cleanly separated and several mechanisms overlap. A single ratification here would likely create a broad, brittle contract surface before the underlying implementations and migration tools exist, so deferring until the architecture is reduced to fewer, more orthogonal invariants would be safer.

CL-A.pick_text: Ratify with revision — the core pattern is correct but specific mechanism (e.g. 2-phase reserve/settle vs single-phase debit, topic naming, fallback on overrun) needs adjustment; specify.
CL-A.rationale: I think centralized ownership is directionally right, but the current reserve/settle protocol needs stronger transactional guarantees and clearer retry semantics. The topic and reaper design are plausible, yet not stable enough to ratify without tightening.

CL-B.pick_text: Ratify with revision — core pattern correct but mechanism (threshold range, default, halt-vs-degraded-output) needs tuning; specify.
CL-B.rationale: The fail-loud idea is sound, but the template is too permissive in metric choice and too vague on when a halt is preferable to degraded output. I would keep the gate, but require stricter defaults and clearer product-class guidance.

CL-C.pick_text: Ratify with revision — pattern correct but coverage (e.g. should require all 3 modes documented even if behavior unchanged, or only delta blocks) needs adjustment.
CL-C.rationale: Explicit mode behavior helps, but requiring the same field on every envelope feels heavy-handed for mode-agnostic agents. I’d prefer a slimmer declaration, with clearer rules about when deltas versus full mode documentation are required.

CL-D.pick_text: Ratify with revision — namespace convention correct but specific topic list (which are P0, which deferred, naming) needs adjustment; specify.
CL-D.rationale: The naming discipline is useful, but the pre-registration list is too broad and mixes true canonical topics with migration placeholders and aliases. I would only ratify after splitting P0 registrations from deferred or transitional names.

CL-E.pick_text: Ratify with revision — helper + pattern correct but specifics (where to check, what to log on violation, who handles ceiling-rejected agents) need adjustment.
CL-E.rationale: A ceiling helper is sensible, but the enforcement order and failure ownership are underspecified and duplicated across orchestrator and agent layers. I would keep the pattern while forcing a single authoritative rejection path and clearer logging semantics.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify with revision — 3-tier cascade correct but specifics (tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, Doppler-key naming) need adjustment.
CL-F.rationale: The fallback concept is solid, but the exact model chain and trigger rules are too opinionated and will age badly as providers change. I would ratify the idea only after making the fallback tiers and key names more abstract and configurable.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Net: mostly revise, not reject outright. Each cluster solves a real gap, but several of them do so by over-specifying cross-cutting mechanics before the implementation contracts and migration tooling are mature.

objections.title: Overly Complex Cost Governance
objections.detail: The Cluster A template introduces a 2-phase reserve/settle mechanism that adds complexity to the cost governance system. This may lead to issues with atomicity and consistency across multiple agents.

objections.title: Data Quality Gate Thresholds
objections.detail: The Cluster B template relies on per-agent threshold defaults and operator overrides. However, it is unclear how these thresholds will be determined and whether they will be effective in practice.

objections.title: Mode-Conditional Behavior Ambiguity
objections.detail: The Cluster C template requires agents to declare their mode behavior, but it is unclear how this will be enforced and whether it will lead to inconsistencies across agents.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the proposed changes are implemented incorrectly, they may lead to a more complex and brittle system that is harder to maintain and debug than the current status quo.
adversarial.precedent: The introduction of a centralized cost governor agent is similar to the design of AWS Cost Explorer, which has been successful in managing costs for AWS users.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: One could argue that the proposed changes are too complex and may introduce new risks and challenges that outweigh their potential benefits. For example, the 2-phase reserve/settle mechanism in Cluster A may lead to issues with atomicity and consistency, while the per-agent threshold defaults in Cluster B may be difficult to determine and maintain.

CL-A.pick_text: Ratify with revision — the core pattern is correct but specific mechanism (e.g. 2-phase reserve/settle vs single-phase debit, topic naming, fallback on overrun) needs adjustment; specify in rationale.
CL-A.rationale: The 2-phase reserve/settle mechanism is a good approach, but it may need adjustments to ensure atomicity and consistency across multiple agents.

CL-B.pick_text: Ratify — configurable per-product threshold + data_quality.insufficient.v1 audit-log topic + halt-not-produce semantics is the right pattern.
CL-B.rationale: The data quality gate is a necessary feature to ensure that agents produce high-quality output, and the proposed template provides a good balance between flexibility and consistency.

CL-C.pick_text: Ratify with revision — pattern correct but coverage (e.g. should require all 3 modes documented even if behavior unchanged, or only delta blocks) needs adjustment.
CL-C.rationale: The mode-conditional behavior template is a good start, but it may need adjustments to ensure that agents are consistent in their mode behavior and that the template is not too rigid or too flexible.

CL-D.pick_text: Ratify — ~30 new topics + §14.1 canonical extension + namespace convention (per-agent + cross-cutting) is the right pattern.
CL-D.rationale: The proposed topic schema extension is necessary to support the new features and agents, and the namespace convention provides a clear and consistent way to organize topics.

CL-E.pick_text: Ratify — getCeiling() helper + ceiling-check-before-act pattern is the right integration with CA-12 v3 §A.2.4 authorityCeilings JSONB.
CL-E.rationale: The proposed authority-ceiling integration template provides a clear and consistent way to enforce authority ceilings across agents and Executors.

CL-F.pick_text: Ratify with revision — 3-tier cascade correct but specifics (tier names, model choices, fallback trigger conditions, Doppler-key naming) need adjustment.
CL-F.rationale: The 3-tier model selection cascade is a good approach, but it may need adjustments to ensure that the tier names, model choices, and fallback trigger conditions are optimal and consistent across agents.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposed changes are generally well-structured and address important issues, but may require some adjustments to ensure consistency and effectiveness across agents and features.

objections.title: Topic proliferation in §14.1
objections.detail: Cluster D adds ~30 new topics to the existing 65-topic catalogue in §14.1 without a live migration test harness. This directly contradicts Batch 2 objection #21 on message bus congestion and risks runtime UNKNOWN_TOPIC errors during incremental agent shipping per MessageSchema.js validation.

objections.title: Dual-authority bypass risk
objections.detail: Cluster E §2.6 permits Agent #26 and #21 to carry [auto_write_internal, requires_human_gate] at the primary layer, bypassing the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling pattern in §15.5. Ceiling checks via getCeiling() occur after BaseAgent.guard(), creating an ordering window for unauthorized writes not present in the status-quo single-authority model.

objections.title: 2-phase reservation deadlock
objections.detail: Cluster A §2.3 reserve/settle against flowai_run_budgets uses Supabase RLS-locked UPDATE without explicit timeout or deadlock detection. AC-CA-2's 100-concurrent test assumes perfect atomicity, yet concurrent pre-dispatch calls from Agents #6/#10/#15 can starve the reaper job and leave reservations orphaned beyond the 10-minute window.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The six-cluster overlay of reservation, quality gates, mode blocks, ceiling lookups and fallback chains can cause more AutoRunner step halts than the prior fragmented self-checks, forcing operators to lower thresholds or disable gates entirely and thereby re-introducing the original budget and data-quality risks at higher operational cost.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal bundles six interdependent canonical templates that each modify the same §14.1 audit catalogue, §15.1 roster wiring and CA-12 authority surfaces. Without a staged pilot on a single shipped agent (e.g. #6) and measured failure-rate data, the cumulative surface area for race conditions, topic collisions and authority creep exceeds the risk of the current fragmented but contained per-agent checks.

CL-A.pick_text: Reject — Cost Governor should not be a separate agent; budget enforcement belongs in the orchestrator or per-agent self-check, not in a centralized authority surface.
CL-A.rationale: Centralizing in Agent #23 adds a new single point of failure and ordering dependency not justified by the Panel quotes.

CL-B.pick_text: Reject — data-quality gate should be enforced earlier (e.g. at ACE crawl boundary) rather than per-agent; the canonical answer is "fix the input gate", not add a per-agent gate.
CL-B.rationale: Per-agent halts fragment UX and duplicate work already possible at the crawl layer per ENTRY 006.

CL-C.pick_text: Reject — mode-conditional behavior should be expressed at the AutoRunner / pipeline layer, not per-agent; agents should be mode-agnostic and the pipeline routes them.
CL-C.rationale: Per-agent §5.4 blocks duplicate the pipeline-mode logic already present in CA-12 v3 §B.2 validation.

CL-D.pick_text: Reject — adding 30 topics at once is over-specification; canonical schema should grow with agent ship, not pre-define before agents are built.
CL-D.rationale: Pre-declaring before any of the 19 agents ship risks schema drift and migration debt.

CL-E.pick_text: Reject — authority ceiling should be enforced at the orchestrator layer (single source of truth), not by each agent calling getCeiling(); per-agent check duplicates enforcement.
CL-E.rationale: Per-Executor getCeiling() calls create the exact enforcement inconsistency the cluster claims to solve.

CL-F.pick_text: Reject — model-budget fallback should not be a spec-level concern; the Orchestra adapter layer already handles model routing and budget cascade should live there entirely.
CL-F.rationale: Spec-level Doppler reads duplicate the existing dispatchWithFallback mechanism in CA-11-A.4.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All clusters increase cross-agent coupling without staged rollout criteria or rollback paths.
